deep.reconstruction:
The page has two parts. The top part writes down the energy of an isotropic elastic body. The lower part is a kinematic computation for a deformation in the (y,z)-plane, first in polar coordinates and then in complex conjugate coordinates.

(A) Elastic energy (top, separated by a horizontal rule).
Riemann writes (left-hand label unclear, possibly -2Ω)
  ∫ [ a(λ1+λ2+λ3)^2 + 2(b−a)(λ2λ3+λ1λ3+λ1λ2) ] ρ dϑ.
Here λ1, λ2, λ3 are the principal extensions (eigenvalues of the strain tensor ε), ρ is the density and dϑ is the volume element. The integrand is a·I1^2 + 2(b−a)·I2, written with the invariants I1 = tr ε and I2 = the sum of the principal 2×2 minors.
Using I1^2 = Σλi^2 + 2·I2 (my filled-in step), this equals (a−b)·Σλi^2 + b·I1^2.
The second line rewrites this in displacement components (u,v,w), using tr(ε^2) = Σ(∂u/∂x)^2 + ½Σ(∂v/∂z+∂w/∂y)^2:
  ½(a−b)[(∂v/∂z+∂w/∂y)^2 + …] + (a−b)[(∂u/∂x)^2 + …] + b(∂u/∂x+∂v/∂y+∂w/∂z)^2.
This is the standard two-constant isotropic strain-energy density μ·tr ε^2 + (λ/2)(tr ε)^2, up to the normalisation of Ω. It corresponds to μ = a−b and λ = 2b, or 2μ = a−b and λ = b if the left side is twice the energy. The factor ρ suggests the energy is taken per unit mass.

(B) Polar coordinates in the cross-section.
Set y = r cos φ, z = r sin φ. Then
  dy = (y/r)dr − z dφ,  dz = (z/r)dr + y dφ,
  r dr = y dy + z dz,  r^2 dφ = −z dy + y dz.
Hence for any function α:
  ∂α/∂y = (y/r)∂α/∂r − (z/r^2)∂α/∂φ,
  ∂α/∂z = (z/r)∂α/∂r + (y/r^2)∂α/∂φ.
The point (r,φ) is displaced to the point with polar coordinates (ρ,ψ); here ρ is reused for the deformed radius, not the density. So
  v = ρ cos ψ − y,  w = ρ sin ψ − z.
Riemann computes the planar dilatation ∂v/∂y + ∂w/∂z. The two crossed-out lines carry out the chain rule term by term. The final, uncrossed result is
  ∂v/∂y + ∂w/∂z = cos(φ−ψ)[∂ρ/∂r + (ρ/r)∂ψ/∂φ] + sin(ψ−φ)[(1/r)∂ρ/∂φ − ρ ∂ψ/∂r] − 2.
I verified this. The −2 comes from the −y and −z terms.

(C) Complex conjugate coordinates.
Set p = y+zi and q = y−zi, so pq = r^2 and p/q = α^2 with α = e^{iφ}. Then
  ∂/∂y = ∂/∂p + ∂/∂q,  ∂/∂z = i(∂/∂p − ∂/∂q).
Applied to the parts ρcosψ and ρsinψ, the −y and −z terms give the −1 on the page:
  ∂v/∂y = ∂v/∂p + ∂v/∂q − 1,
  ∂w/∂z = i(∂w/∂p − ∂w/∂q) − 1.
The combinations π = v+wi and χ = v−wi give π+χ = 2v and π−χ = 2wi, and Riemann notes
  π(1+i)/2 + χ(1−i)/2 = v − w,
  π(1−i)/2 + χ(1+i)/2 = v + w.
He begins forming ∂(v+w)/∂p + ∂(v+w)/∂q − 1 − i. He then transforms ∂/∂p and ∂/∂q to (r,α). By my computation:
  ∂/∂p = (1/(2α))∂/∂r + (1/(2r))∂/∂α,
  ∂/∂q = (α/2)∂/∂r − (α^2/(2r))∂/∂α.
This is the source of the factors (1±i)/(2α) and (1∓i)α/2 multiplying ∂π/∂r and ∂χ/∂r in the last two lines.
That final transformation is left unfinished and is only partly legible. The aim seems to be expressing the strain components of a plane (cross-sectional) finite or polar displacement in complex form, plausibly for torsion or deformation of a cylinder within the energy functional of (A).
errors: No mathematical errors detected in the legible steps.
Notation clash: ρ is the density in the energy integral but the radius of the deformed point in part (B)/(C).
The last lines (chain rule to r, α with factors (1±i)/(2α), (1∓i)α/2) are fragmentary and cannot be fully checked; they are consistent with ∂r/∂p = 1/(2α) and ∂r/∂q = α/2.
The normalisation of the energy (−2Ω vs Ω) is unclear, so the identification of a, b with Lamé constants is fixed only up to a factor of 2.

results.what: Isotropic elastic energy density written via principal strains as a·I1^2 + 2(b−a)·I2 = (a−b)tr ε^2 + b(tr ε)^2, and in displacement-gradient form
results.modern_name: Strain-energy density of isotropic linear elasticity (Lamé form, invariant form)

results.what: Polar-coordinate chain rule and the planar dilatation of the map (r,φ) → (ρ,ψ): cos(φ−ψ)[ρ_r + ρψ_φ/r] + sin(ψ−φ)[ρ_φ/r − ρψ_r] − 2
results.modern_name: Divergence of a displacement field in polar coordinates (deformed-position description)

results.what: Complex conjugate coordinates p=y+iz, q=y−iz with ∂/∂y = ∂_p+∂_q, ∂/∂z = i(∂_p−∂_q), and complex displacement combinations π=v+iw, χ=v−iw
results.modern_name: Wirtinger derivatives / complex representation of plane displacements (precursor of the Kolosov–Muskhelishvili formalism)
results.usually_credited_to: Wirtinger (1927) for the derivatives as a calculus; Kolosov (1909) and Muskhelishvili for complex methods in plane elasticity

deep.surprise_reason: The elasticity energy and the polar chain rule are textbook material of the time. Riemann's use of conjugate variables x±iy is well known from his 1851 dissertation. Applying them to displacement components in plane elasticity is a mildly interesting early instance, but no stress-function or Kolosov-type result is reached, and the computation breaks off.

transcription_corrections: Line 1 of the polar block should read dy = dr·y/r − z dφ (the '[?]' term is dy).

The final uncrossed long line almost certainly begins '∂v/∂y + ∂w/∂z =' rather than '∂u/∂x +'. Likewise the crossed-out lines begin '∂v/∂y + ∂w/∂z =' with '=' rather than '+'. The trailing '−2' confirms that both the v and w contributions are included.

Second line: the '[-...-]' between the two bracketed groups is a struck-out coefficient, leaving '+ (a−b)[(∂u/∂x)² + …]'. The first bracket is ½(a−b)[(∂v/∂z+∂w/∂y)² + …], i.e. a sum of squares, not a difference.
'v + wi = y + zi' and 'p = (ρ/r) sin α', '1 = ρ/r' are tentative. They are probably side jottings relating the deformed position ρe^{iψ} to p = y+zi, and are not reliable as transcribed.
The left label of the first line ('−2Ω') is uncertain; only the integral itself is clearly legible.
